item.title: When My Body Stopped Working: How I Found Hope Again
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Essential for personal growth and resilience, with clear and compelling storytelling.

“We must be willing to let go of the life we planned so as to have the life that is waiting for us.”

Ten years ago, my life underwent a catastrophic software crash.

I was a typically active, healthy thirteen-year-old boy growing up in Nottinghamshire. Then, within a matter of days, my entire reality completely shattered.

My body simply stopped working. I lost the ability to walk, my speech vanished, my hands stopped responding, and I became completely incontinent.

I was in the hospital for months. Medical teams were utterly baffled. I was subjected to endless clinical scans, lumbar punctures, and tests, but a strange pattern emerged: physically, my brain and body hardware were completely perfect.

Eventually, doctors diagnosed me with severe Functional Neurological Disorder (FND). They explained it by using a computer analogy—my brain’s physical hardware was fine, but the software had completely crashed, sending scrambled signals to my body.

For three long years, I was completely bedridden and was non-verbal for a year, trapped inside a body that had simply shut down.

When you lose everything within days, the psychological isolation is suffocating. I spent months waiting for a miracle pill or a doctor to tell me they had fixed the glitch, but that day never came.

I fell into a deeply dark place, feeling completely detached from the world outside my window. The life I had planned as a teenager was gone, and I felt utterly powerless.

For six months I can only describe it as my mind switched off, and I didn’t know who or what anything was.

One afternoon, while my brain functioning had improved and I could understand what was happening around me, a realization hit me. I couldn’t control the scrambled signals in my nervous system, but I could control how I reacted to the darkness.

I realized that waiting for a massive, overnight miracle was keeping me trapped. I needed to stop looking at the top of the mountain and just focus on the next single inch.

I started finding tiny, unconventional anchors to keep my mind alive. I built a fierce, quiet goal to one day visit London, spending hours visualizing the city and planning out journeys I wanted to take if I ever got out of that bed.

Slowly, over years of grueling emotional and physical rehabilitation, the software started to reboot. I remember the first time I moved a finger slightly. It was a very small achievement, but it was a huge milestone, as at one time I was unable to move any part of my body.

In time, I learned how to communicate again, how to move my hands, how to sit up, and how to navigate the world from a wheelchair.

Today, at twenty-three, I have successfully traveled to over 120 towns and cities across the UK. This year, to mark a decade of living with FND, I stood up out of my wheelchair in the middle of London and had twenty photos of me out of my wheelchair—a milestone that felt entirely impossible when I was paralyzed in that hospital bed. When I was well enough, I also achieved other goals, such as meeting some of my favorite celebrities.

Going through a sudden, life-altering interruption taught me a profound lesson about the nature of hope. Hope isn’t a passive wish for things to go back to how they used to be; it is an active choice to find meaning in the reality you have right now.

If your life has recently experienced its own version of a software crash, here is what my journey through the dark taught me about rebuilding from scratch:

Focus on the micro milestones.

When a crisis shatters your world, looking at the big picture can feel completely overwhelming. Break your days down into microscopic goals—focusing on just breathing through the next hour, reading one page of a book, or moving a single finger. Celebrate those tiny victories fiercely, because they are the building blocks of your recovery.

Find your mental anchors.

When your physical reality is restricted, your mind doesn’t have to be. Find a dream or a goal that sparks your curiosity or brings you comfort, even if it feels completely out of reach from a hospital bed. Give your brain a positive destination to travel to when your body is stuck. I found goal setting really helpful.

Release the life you thought you’d have.

The greatest suffering often comes from fighting reality and mourning the blueprint of the life we planned. Healing truly began for me when I stopped fighting my disability and instead accepted it as a new starting line. For me, that acceptance came the first time I was well enough to sit in a wheelchair. It felt like freedom to me, and I started to see FND not as something that had trapped me but as part of my life and something that had given me a great sense of determination I didn’t know I had.

Reclaiming your independence doesn’t mean erasing your challenges; it means choosing to thrive alongside them.

About Liam Virgo

Liam Virgo is a twenty-three-year-old British disability advocate, writer, and campaigner raising vital awareness for Functional Neurological Disorder (FND). After spending his teenage years bedridden and paralyzed, he now documents his rehabilitation and accessible travel adventures as a wheelchair user. You can follow his ongoing journey and travel discoveries across the UK on Instagram at @liamloveslondon.

item.title: Tidal Is the First Streaming Platform to Ban AI Music
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Important for understanding the impact of AI on music and streaming platforms.

You have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service. If you own an iPhone and a Mac, you might be tempted by Apple Music; if you have more friends on Spotify, you may feel that's the best platform for you. But if your goal is avoiding AI music as much as humanly possible, there appears to be a new uncontested winner: Tidal.

Tidal will soon remove all AI-generated songs

On Tuesday, Tidal announced plans to ban AI music from its platform entirely. Starting Dec. 9, the company will begin taking steps to remove music it believes is entirely made with AI. Tidal says it thinks the move “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”

This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music. Back in July, the company announced that it would start labeling songs completely made with AI, as well as remove tracks it found to be "fraudulent and deceptive." Other platforms have similar policies, or are rolling out similar features. Apple Music, for example, is working on AI labels for its app, too, and Spotify has pushed back on AI to some degree. However, this most recent move makes Tidal the first music streaming service to outright ban AI-generated music from its catalog.

Robert Anderson, Tidal's Music Lead, posted on X about the change. According to Anderson, Tidal identified 43% of the tracks it received in the last 90 days were AI-generated. Per the company's plan, Tidal will remove 29 million songs by the beginning of 2027, roughly 80,000 to 85,000 removals per day. Some 96% of Tidal's AI-generated songs have zero plays whatsoever.

Other streaming services still allow AI-generated music (for now)

I wouldn't be surprised to see other music streaming services follow suit, particularly Apple Music. Despite rolling out AI-powered features over the past couple of years, including Apple Music's AI-generated playlists, Apple has taken some stands against AI-generated material in general. The latest Apple TV intro was shot in-camera with practical effects, in an era where the company could have easily generated something with AI. If other companies plan to follow Tidal's lead here, my money's on Apple being first in line.

However, as it stands, Tidal is the only streaming service that supports this initiative. Soon enough, it'll be the sole music app you can use with near-zero ambiguity that the music you're listening to was at least mostly created by humans. (What a sentence.) Avoiding AI-generated music can be tricky, frustrating, and, frankly, exhausting. If that's important to you, Tidal might just be your new pick.

item.title: AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Critical for understanding privacy concerns with AI and Signal chats.

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

In a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

How to limit AI from reading your Signal chats

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

Users on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

item.title: Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Good for tech enthusiasts and those interested in Black Friday deals.

Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Nintendo's early Black Friday deals

Last Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World Bundle for $499.99 (save $50)

Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.00, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:

Donkey Kong Bananza for $49.99 (save $20)

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $20 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

Kirby Air Riders for $49.99 (save $20)

Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original launched all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $49.99.

Metroid Prime 4: Beyond for $49 (save up to $30)

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails for $69.99 for a physical copy on Switch 2, but Nintendo is selling it for $49 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 for $48.97 (save $20)

Super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The company offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $48.97 before Black Friday.

Super Mario Party: Jamboree for $59.99 (save $20)

Nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in New York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

Black Friday 2026 FAQs

When do Nintendo’s Black Friday deals start and end?

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

Which Nintendo games are on sale for Black Friday?

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

Is the Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle worth $499.99?

Yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

Why it is here: Informative for those looking for early Black Friday tech deals.

Retailers and brands are churning out early Black Friday deals already, including the likes of Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Samsung, and others. If you're waiting around for Friday, Nov. 27 to do all of your shopping, you might miss out on some deals and unnecessarily make the day more stressful than it needs to be. If you're a Sam's Club member, you have access to many early Black Friday deals worth checking out. I spent some time combing through their website and rounded up my favorite tech deals below.

Sam’s Club Speaker and Soundbar Black Friday Deals

Bose SoundLink Flex SE (2nd Gen) For $89 / Save $50

The Bose SoundLink Flex SE is a portable Bluetooth speaker with an IP67 waterproof rating. The speaker even floats in the water, so you can bring it with you into the pool. While it doesn't offer full EQ customization in its companion app, the sound has rich bass depth and clear highs out of the box. It also features a speakerphone, allowing you to take calls and speak with it. It's light and portable, and the Bluetooth 5.3 supports multipoint connectivity and SBC, AAC, and aptX codecs. You can get the Bose 2nd Generation SoundLink Flex SE for $89 (originally $139).

Skullcandy Stomp XL Max for $99 / Save $100

Skullcandy makes fun speakers and headphones, although they're not designed for audiophiles (their sound signature is very bass-heavy). Their Skullcandy Stomp XL Max is their attempt at making a portable party speaker. It comes with two wireless mics, making it a great option for karaoke. It holds 12 hours of battery life (up to 20 hours with certain settings), has an IPX5 water resistance rating, and has LED lights that sync to the music. You can get it for $99 (originally $199).

Samsung HW-Q65F 5.1 Channel Soundbar For $299 / Save $100

Getting a soundbar can exponentially improve anyone's entertainment system, but a 5.1 system with rear speakers and a subwoofer takes it to the next level. The Samsung HW-Q65F 5.1 Channel Soundbar is $299 (originally $399), and it's a wireless setup that will keep the harmony of "too many cables" in the house. It supports Dolby Atmos and DTS Virtual:X to give you a 3D audio feel, and it has a dialogue feature that will let you hear the whispers.

Sam’s Club Laptop Black Friday Deals

HP OmniBook 7 Flip 16-inch for $699 / Save $200

These kinds of sales are always a good time to upgrade laptops. If you're looking for a powerful computer that is well-rounded, consider the 16-inch HP OmniBook 7 Flip going for $699 (originally $899). This laptop comes with an Intel Ultra 5 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 16GB of RAM (which, honestly, is the minimum anyone should be buying in 2026).

HP OmniBook 3 17.3-inch for $649 / Save $350

If you need a bigger screen, the 17.3-inch HP OmniBook 3 is a good choice for a bit less money at $649 (originally $999). It comes with an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor, 512GB of SSD, and 12GB of RAM. Part of the bigger screen means a bigger keyboard, so if you deal with numbers a lot, you'd likely appreciate the numeric pad.

Sam’s Club Gaming Black Friday Deals

ASUS TUF F16 Gaming Laptop for $1,149 / Save $250

If you want your laptop strictly for gaming, the ASUS TUF F16 Gaming laptop is $1,149 (originally $1,399). With an Intel Core 7 processor and the RTX 5060 graphics card, you'll be well set up to tackle heavy games. It comes with a 165Hz refresh rate, Advanced Arc Flow fans and vents to keep your machine cool, and 16GB DDR5 RAM to keep your loads short.

MSI 31.5-inch Curved Gaming Monitor For $129 / Save $50

Gaming monitors can get expensive quickly, but you can get decent options on a budget. A great example is the 31.5-inch MSi gaming monitor selling for $129 (originally $179). It has a 250Hz refresh rate and a 1ms response time to make gaming smoother. There's also AMD FreeSync Premium to get rid of tearing and stuttering.

Sam’s Club TV Black Friday Deals

Vizio 58-inch Quantum QLED for $178 / Save $120

Budget TVs get big discounts during Black Friday, and the 58-inch Vizio QLED TV is one of them. You can get one for $178 (originally $298), and it supports Dolby Vision HDR for better color and contrast. The operating system is the Vizio OS, but of course, you can always change it with a TV dongle if you prefer a different one.

Samsung 65-inch QN90H Neo QLED Mini LED For $1,197.99 / Save $300

If you prefer to splurge for a better QLED but still get a good deal, the 65-inch Samsung QN90H QLED TV at $1,197.99 (originally $1,497.99) is a great option. It upscales lower-resolution pictures to 4K with AI. It works for gaming with its 144Hz refresh rate, and because the operating system is Tizen OS, it comes with Samsung TV Plus, which brings over 2,700 free channels. The TV also comes with Dolby Atmos, so you can hear audio with a 3D effect as the audio follows objects around the display.

Vizio 100-inch Quantum QLED For $1,198 / Save $300

A 100-inch TV makes a statement: You take your entertainment system seriously. The 100-inch Vizio QLED TV is a budget-friendly option with a $300 discount, currently going for $1,198 (originally $1,498). This TV supports Dolby Vision HDR for more vivid images and has hundreds of free channels with the Vizio OS.

Sam’s Club Black Friday FAQs

What stores have the best sales on Black Friday?

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Why it is here: Useful for gaming enthusiasts seeking early Black Friday deals.

Getting your gaming gear fix during the holiday shopping season is an annual tradition, but it’s more crucial this year than ever. The RAM shortage has driven up all electronics prices, right when the biggest game of all time arrives after a 13-year wait. So any discount you can score can have a big impact on your wallet. Before the main event starts, you can get started with some early Black Friday gaming deals here.

Game consoles are obviously more expensive than they used to be, even when they came out years ago. But bundle deals are still some of the best way to shave some cash off the sticker price. item.title: The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Practical for last-minute gift shopping tips.

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

Sometimes the gift is in the delivery

With the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

And focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Instant purchase digital gifts

Digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:

Libro.fm subscription

If you have an audiobook lover on your list, gifting a subscription to Libro.fm. It can be ordered instantly and lets users access hundreds of thousands of audiobooks. Bonus: Libro doesn't market or promote AI-narrated books, and a percentage of the subscription fee goes to a local independent bookstore the subscriber chooses. In 2027, the service plans to expand to e-books too. Include a note that says something like, "I know how much you love discovering new stories. Now you can explore as many as you like—just make sure you tell me what you find!” Boom! Mission accomplished.

Gift cards that aren't impersonal

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Making generic gift cards seem thoughtful

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

- Pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

- Include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”

- Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Subscription boxes with instant confirmation emails

Sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:

- SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

- SpiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

- Mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

- Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

- Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Send a message from a celebrity

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

Experiential gifts

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

- Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

- Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

- Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.…
